Detailed Description

Doubly linked list for collisions into hashtables.

This list is a doubly linked list mainly targeted for handling collisions into a hashtable, but usable also as a generic list.

The main feature of this list is to require only one pointer to represent the list, compared to a classic implementation requiring both head and tail pointers. This reduces the memory usage in hashtables.

Another feature is to support the insertion at the end of the list. This allows storing collisions in a stable order, meaning that equal elements preserve their insertion order.

To initialize the list, you have to call tommy_list_init(), or to simply assign to it 0, as an empty list is represented by the 0 value.

tommy_list list;
tommy_list_init(&list); // initializes the list

To insert elements in the list you have to call tommy_list_insert_tail() or tommy_list_insert_head() for each element. In the insertion call you have to specify the address of the node and the address of the element. The address of the element is used to initialize the tommy_node::data field of the node.

struct element {
int value;
// other fields
tommy_node node;
};
struct element* elem = malloc(sizeof(struct element)); // creates the element
elem->value = ...; // initializes the element
tommy_list_insert_tail(&list, &elem->node, elem); // inserts the element

Inserts an element at the tail of a list.
Definition: tommylist.h:331

To iterate over all the elements in the list you have to call tommy_list_head() to get the head of the list and follow the tommy_node::next pointer until 0.

tommy_node* i = tommy_list_head(&list);
while (i) {
struct element* elem = i->data; // gets the element pointer
printf("%d\n", elem->value); // process the element
i = i->next; // go to the next element
}

To iterate backward, start at tommy_list_tail() and use tommy_list_prev(). Do not follow tommy_node::prev directly past the head, as it points to the tail.

tommy_node* i = tommy_list_tail(&list);
while (i) {
struct element* elem = i->data;
printf("%d\n", elem->value);
i = tommy_list_prev(&list, i);
}

Iterators are pointers to nodes contained in the list. Inserting elements or removing other nodes between iterator calls does not invalidate pointers to nodes that remain in the list. Subsequent next/prev calls use the current contents and ordering; inserted elements may become visible and removed elements are skipped.

Removing the pointed node invalidates its use as an iterator, even if its storage has not been freed. To continue traversal after removing the current node, obtain the next or previous node before removal.

tommy_node* i = tommy_list_head(&list);
while (i) {
tommy_node* next = i->next; // obtain the next node before removal
if (condition) {
tommy_list_remove_existing(&list, i);
free(i->data); // safe to deallocate
}
i = next;
}

Concurrent traversal and modification require external synchronization.

To reorder existing elements, use tommy_list_move_head(), tommy_list_move_tail() or tommy_list_reverse(). To split a list or transfer elements between lists, use tommy_list_split(), tommy_list_prepend(), tommy_list_splice_before() and tommy_list_splice_after(). These operations preserve the element pointers and do not allocate memory.

tommy_list second;
tommy_list_init(&second);
// transfers node and all following nodes to second
tommy_list_split(&list, node, &second);
// appends the transferred nodes back to list
tommy_list_concat(&list, &second);

Two lists sorted with the same comparison function can be merged with tommy_list_merge(). The merge is stable.

To destroy the list you have to remove all the elements, as the list is completely in-place and it doesn't allocate memory. This can be done with the tommy_list_foreach() function.

// deallocates all the elements iterating the list
tommy_list_foreach(&list, free);
tommy_list_clear(&list); // resets the list before reuse

typedef struct tommy_builder_struct tommy_builder

Temporary list builder with an embedded sentinel.

Initialize with tommy_builder_init() and finish with tommy_list_concat_builder(). Keep the builder at the same address until finalization, as node links refer to its sentinel.

◆ tommy_list_split()

void tommy_list_split ( tommy_list *  list,
tommy_node *  node,
tommy_list *  second 
)

Splits a list before the specified node.

The list retains the nodes preceding the specified node. The second list receives the specified node and all following nodes. The order of the elements is preserved. The tommy_node::data and tommy_node::index fields are left unchanged.

Parameters
listThe list to split.
nodeThe first node to transfer. The node must be in the list, or 0 to leave list unchanged and set second to 0. Specifying the head transfers the whole list.
secondOutput list receiving node and all following nodes. It must be distinct from list and need not be initialized. Its previous value is overwritten. Any previously referenced nodes are left unchanged and are not deallocated.
Note
This operation is O(1).

◆ tommy_list_merge()

TOMMY_API void tommy_list_merge ( tommy_list *  first,
tommy_list *  second,
tommy_compare_func *  cmp 
)

Merges two sorted lists.

Both lists must be sorted using the same comparison function. The merge is stable: equal elements from the first list precede those from the second list, and the relative order within each list is preserved. The tommy_node::data and tommy_node::index fields are left unchanged.

Parameters
firstThe destination list, receiving the sorted result.
secondThe source list. After this call the list content is undefined, and you should not use it anymore. The lists must be distinct and must not share nodes.
cmpCompare function called with two elements. The function should return <0 if the first element is less than the second, ==0 if equal, and >0 if greater. It must not modify the lists.
Note
This operation is O(n+m), or O(1) when one list is empty or the ranges can be concatenated directly. It uses O(1) auxiliary space.

◆ tommy_list_foreach()

void tommy_list_foreach ( tommy_list *  list,
tommy_foreach_func *  func 
)

Calls the specified function for each element in the list.

You cannot add or remove elements from the inside of the callback, but can use it to deallocate them.

tommy_list list;
// initializes the list
tommy_list_init(&list);
...
// creates an element
struct element* elem = malloc(sizeof(struct element));
...
// insert it in the list
tommy_list_insert_tail(&list, &elem->node, elem);
...
// deallocates all the elements iterating the list
tommy_list_foreach(&list, free);
tommy_list_clear(&list); // resets the list before reuse

If the callback frees the elements, the list retains dangling node pointers. Call tommy_list_clear() or tommy_list_init() before reusing it. The list has no storage to release.

Parameters
listThe list.
funcFunction to call with each element.

Calls the specified function with an argument for each element in the list.
